title: Xpo1 gain in caudal neurons induces Arrdc3/Slc16a6/Vamp2/Sun2 and represses RNA-processing transcripts without mimicking selinexor-like inhibition
exact_observed_result: Xpo1 targeting increased Xpo1 RNA in the strongest responsive classes and produced a bidirectional module: Arrdc3, Slc16a6, Vamp2, and Sun2 rose while Snrnp70, Arglu1, Pabpn1, and Srsf-family rows fell. A WNT/TGF-beta/p53 sentinel panel produced zero FDR<0.05 rows in the five responsive classes.
biological_interpretation: This is an Xpo1-transcript gain state coupled to RNA-processing repression and is directionally distinct from pharmacologic CRM1/XPO1 inhibition by selinexor.

support.description: Five caudal or subcortical classes carried FDR-supported Xpo1 module rows.
The recurrent arm contained Arrdc3 in six cell types, Slc16a6 and Snrnp70 in five, and no FDR induction of inhibitor cargo sentinels.

caveats: Two Arrdc3-only rows occurred without detectable Xpo1 target-transcript gain, so Arrdc3 alone is not a complete engagement marker.
The selinexor comparison used sentinel mRNAs only and cannot exclude protein relocalization or drug-specific cargo effects.

prior_expectation.summary: CRM1/XPO1 is a Ran-dependent nuclear export receptor and a clinical Exportin-1 inhibitor target; the neuronal data instead represent excess Xpo1 transcript.

citations.citation: ChEMBL Exportin-1 target and selinexor mechanism records.
